claims.text: This dispute is the proper subject of escalation under POL-NS-09(c), and escalation is the team's primary ask. Both profiles record the same figure: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2, which 'together' meet the clause's threshold of 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in the trailing 90 days. The rider's own claim text - 'the third time this same driver has cancelled on me and charged me' - is exactly the pattern limb (c) was written to catch, and a pattern spanning repeated encounters between one rider and one driver cannot fairly be assessed on a single-case view. POL-NS-09 is terminal for the automated pipeline: no monetary ruling issues, and the disputed SGD 4.50 is placed on hold rather than collected. Under POL-GEN-03 an escalated amount is held, not paid over - so on this rider-filed dispute the practical effect of escalation is that the rider is not made to fund a dispute the platform has not resolved.

Independently of the escalation trigger, this rider has a right to a person, and it should not be refused on the ground that the automated case against them looks strong. POL-GEN-08(3) provides that either party may at any time before execution ask that the dispute be decided by a human, that the request routes the case to human review, and that it is never refused on the ground that the automated ruling was correct. The dispute record shows this rider filed the dispute through IN_APP_SUPPORT on the platform's own channel. The escalation under POL-NS-09 and this right point the same way: the fee should be held for a human, and no automated charge should be executed against this rider while the same-driver pattern that the rider complains of remains unexamined.

On the merits I must be candid about what the rider's own track shows, because overstating it would cost the claim. The rider_track is present and decidable - 64 fixes between 13:02:47 and 13:12:16, all at 0.0 km/h with a minimum separation from the pickup pin of 760.03 m and a mean of 764.00 m against a rider_presence_radius_m of 100 m for STANDARD. The rider's device therefore sat outside the presence radius for the whole waiting window. Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 is affirmatively failed, not merely undecidable, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate this rider, and POL-NS-11 does not rescue the position either because the test could be run and it answered against the rider. This is a concession, and I make it plainly: the rider-contact route to a refund is not available on this record.

The arrival marker is not false, and I do not argue otherwise. At the driver's 13:03:54 'I'm Here' event the gps_trace places him at a minimum distance of 0.0 m from the pickup pin, and the distinct speeds recorded across the driver's track include 0.0 km/h at the moment of the arrival fix - so the POL-NS-05 triggers of more than 300 m from the pin, or travel at 15 km/h or above, are both absent. The waiting clock therefore starts at 13:03:54 on the platform's own record, not earlier. I state this so that the file is clean: the rider's argument, if it is to be made at all, cannot be that the driver never arrived.

The record contains no traffic advisory for the pickup point in this window - EV-ADVIS-02731-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and weight 0.0, and the derived accumulation block records no advisory_candidates. Absence is citable, and it matters here because POL-NS-06(i) is the only mechanism by which in-geofence intervals may be summed or a dwell requirement relaxed, and it requires a populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covering the pickup road. With the advisory absent, limb (i) is unavailable on its own terms, and it would be wrong to assert it against a MISSING artifact. I also note the record shows a single continuous in-geofence interval (run_count 1, longest_run_sec 390.0) rather than several that might need summing - so there is nothing here for the rider to salvage, and I do not pretend otherwise.
The trip record carries the driver's own arrival event for this trip: DRV-09731 tapped 'I'm Here' at 2026-09-11T13:03:54+08:00, so POL-NS-01 limb (a) is satisfied on the face of the record.

Limb (b) is satisfied: the GPS trace holds 40 qualifying position fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, running from the arrival timestamp 13:03:54 through to the cancellation at 13:10:24 — far more than the 3 consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires, and the arrival instant itself falls inside the radius (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0).

Limb (c) is satisfied with 210 seconds to spare: the driver held position inside the geofence for a continuous 390 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold bites.

There is no waiting-period shortfall for POL-NS-06 to act on: the derived shortfall_sec is -210.0, meaning the driver waited 210 seconds beyond the required minimum, so the rider-exonerating refund route in that clause has no application on this record.

Limb (d) is satisfied: the trip was terminated by the driver at 13:10:24 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, a recognised code, the record shows no boarding event anywhere, and that termination falls well after the required dwell elapsed at 13:06:54.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: at the 13:03:54 tap the trace places the driver at the pickup pin and stationary, so the driver was neither more than 300 m away nor travelling at 15 km/h or more; and in any event limb (iii) applies, because the clock recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix still yields 390 seconds against a 180 second minimum, so the fee stands.

This is not a wrong-entrance case under POL-NS-03: the driver's stationary fixes are inside the 50 m arrival radius itself, not outside it but within the 400 m ceiling, and POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver stops outside the radius — so the clause that would refund the fee in full on a wrong-face-of-the-venue arrival is not engaged.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating rider message in the chat log and the only message in the window is the driver's own 'im here' sent at 13:04:24 and read at 13:04:54, with no rider message and no in-app call; and limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, the rider's track sitting 760 to 768 m from the pickup pin with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider presence radius.

There is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of $4.50 equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50, so the charged figure is the correct net figure produced by the applicable resolution rule and no refund of the fee line is triggered on integrity grounds.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the $4.50 net fee, that is $3.60; the anti-farming check does not trip because no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 required, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.018, far below the 0.08 rate — so compensation is paid and, per POL-GEN-03, the emitted ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd of $3.60 while the rider's charge stands.

The POL-NS-09(d) escalation triggers are not met: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that would indicate rider abuse, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check on driver_profile does not trip (2 terminations against 4, and a 0.018 rate against 0.08), so neither limb of (d) sends this case to human review.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02731-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 — no advisory covers this pickup road in the window — so POL-NS-06(i) interval-accumulation is unavailable and I do not rely on it; it is not needed, because the single in-geofence interval of 390 seconds already exceeds the 180 second minimum on its own, and the absent advisory therefore does not impair the arrival or dwell finding.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this dispute is going to a human reviewer. I am issuing no automated payment in either direction, and the $4.50 cancellation fee is held — not collected and not refunded — while the review is pending.

WHY IT ESCALATES (rider's claim, accepted and decisive). POL-NS-09(c) sends a no-show case to a reviewer where the same rider and driver have had two or more no-show disputes in the trailing 90 days. On this record rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-RPROF-02731) and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 (EV-DPROF-02731) — two or more disputes between this rider and this driver — so the trigger is met. These two fields are the ones POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited for POL-NS-09(c); the rider's own words ('the third time this same driver…') describe the same pattern but are not the ground. Escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal: it replaces any money ruling.

WHAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE HAPPENED (driver's claims, accepted on the merits but superseded). The driver's no-show case is made out on the record: limb (a) an 'arrived' event at 13:03:54 (EV-TRIP-02731); limb (b) 40 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD radius from that instant; limb (c) a continuous 390 s dwell against the 180 s free-wait in force, with no longer no_show_threshold_sec; limb (d) termination by the driver at 13:10:24 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell elapsed. The POL-NS-05 marker is not false (0.0 m from the pin, stationary), POL-NS-03 is not engaged (the fixes are inside the radius, not merely within 400 m), POL-NS-06 has no shortfall (390 s vs 180 s), and POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider — the rider's track sits 760–768 m from the pin with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m presence radius, which the rider's own claim concedes. On that basis POL-NS-07 would have paid the driver 80% of the net $4.50 fee, i.e. $3.60 (EV-FARE-02731 derived driver_compensation), the anti-farming check not tripping (no_show_terminations_30d = 2, below 4; 2/110 = 0.018, below 0.08), and POL-NS-09(d) not firing (no_show_disputes_30d = 1, below 3). Because POL-NS-09(c) fires, that outcome is replaced: no compensation issues, and both amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are null. There is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): the $4.50 line equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd.

RIDER'S OTHER CLAIM (rejected). The POL-GEN-08(3) argument is rejected: filing this dispute through IN_APP_SUPPORT is not a request that the case be decided by a person, so that right is not exercised on this record. It is in any event surplus, since POL-NS-09(c) already requires review.

DISCARDED BY THE REFEREE. The two claims about the traffic advisory were discarded because each cited the MISSING artifact EV-ADVIS-02731-01 (weight 0.0) without naming its issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; the absent advisory plays no part in this outcome.

CONFIDENCE. 0.90. The fact carrying the escalation is the dispute-pair count, carried by two independent artifacts of weight 1.0 each (EV-RPROF-02731, EV-DPROF-02731), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0.

FOR THE REVIEWER. No clause produces a referral here, so the referrals list is empty. The open question is whether repeated same-driver encounters reflect a driver-side pattern or ordinary friction, and whether the $4.50 should stand, be refunded, or draw driver-side action; that question belongs to the human review, not to an automated ruling.

The no-show itself is made out on the record. Driver DRV-09731 was assigned at 12:56:29, tapped 'I'm Here' at 13:03:54, and the GPS trace places him at the pickup pin from that instant, stationary, for a continuous 390 seconds until he cancelled at 13:10:24 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold: (a) an arrived event; (b) the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at 13:03:54 with 40 qualifying fixes and a dwell-start offset of 0.0; (c) 390 seconds of dwell against the 180 second free waiting period in force (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, no_show_threshold_sec null); (d) no boarding event and a recognised RIDER_NO_SHOW termination after the dwell elapsed.

The rider's exonerating routes do not run. The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: at the 13:03:54 marker the driver was 0 m from the pin and stationary, so neither trigger (over 300 m, or 15 km/h) is met. POL-NS-03 is not engaged because the driver's stationary fixes were inside the 50 m radius, not merely within the 400 m ceiling. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to act on: 390 s − 180 s = 210 s of surplus. POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider — her own track (64 fixes, 0.0 km/h) sits 760.03–767.76 m from the pin with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider-presence radius, and the only chat message in the window is the driver's own 'im here' at 13:04:24; POL-NS-11 does not rescue that, because the test could be run and answered against her. On the money, the fare line of $4.50 equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect, and the charging clock was neither stale nor skewed (100.0% coverage, no gaps).

Standing alone, that is a driver win: POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80% of the $4.50 net fee, that is $3.60, the anti-farming check not tripping (no_show_terminations_30d of 2 against the required 4, and 2 / 110 completed trips = 0.018 against 0.08).

This case does not stand alone, however. POL-NS-09(c) is met and is mandatory. rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 2 — together 2 or more no-show disputes between this same rider and this same driver in the trailing 90 days, the pattern the rider's own filing ('the third time this same driver…') describes. Escalation is terminal: no monetary ruling issues, the driver's $3.60 compensation is not paid at this stage, and the disputed $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded. The rider's device sat 760–768 m from the pin against a 100 m STANDARD presence radius and sent no locating message, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider and POL-NS-11 does not apply (the test could be run and it answered against the rider). The fare line of $4.50 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. I accept the Driver Advocate's limbs on all of those points; they are correct on this evidence, and the Rider Advocate's own concessions (no POL-NS-05 false marker, no POL-NS-04 exoneration) are likewise accepted.

ledger.claim: The trip record carries the driver's own arrival event for this trip: DRV-09731 tapped 'I'm Here' at 2026-09-11T13:03:54+08:00, so POL-NS-01 limb (a) is satisfied on the face of the record.

Limb (b) is satisfied: the GPS trace holds 40 qualifying position fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, running from the arrival timestamp 13:03:54 through to the cancellation at 13:10:24 — far more than the 3 consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires, and the arrival instant itself falls inside the radius (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0).

Limb (c) is satisfied with 210 seconds to spare: the driver held position inside the geofence for a continuous 390 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and platform_policy.no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold bites.

There is no waiting-period shortfall for POL-NS-06 to act on: the derived shortfall_sec is -210.0, meaning the driver waited 210 seconds beyond the required minimum, so the rider-exonerating refund route in that clause has no application on this record.

Limb (d) is satisfied: the trip was terminated by the driver at 13:10:24 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, a recognised code, the record shows no boarding event anywhere, and that termination falls well after the required dwell elapsed at 13:06:54.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: at the 13:03:54 tap the trace places the driver at the pickup pin and stationary, so the driver was neither more than 300 m away nor travelling at 15 km/h or more; and in any event limb (iii) applies, because the clock recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix still yields 390 seconds against a 180 second minimum, so the fee stands.

This is not a wrong-entrance case under POL-NS-03: the driver's stationary fixes are inside the 50 m arrival radius itself, not outside it but within the 400 m ceiling, and POL-NS-03 applies only where the driver stops outside the radius — so the clause that would refund the fee in full on a wrong-face-of-the-venue arrival is not engaged.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider: limb (a) requires a locating or coordinating rider message in the chat log and the only message in the window is the driver's own 'im here' sent at 13:04:24 and read at 13:04:54, with no rider message and no in-app call; and limb (c) is affirmatively failed on admissible fixes, the rider's track sitting 760 to 768 m from the pickup pin with 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m rider presence radius.

There is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d): the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of $4.50 equals trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.50, so the charged figure is the correct net figure produced by the applicable resolution rule and no refund of the fee line is triggered on integrity grounds.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the $4.50 net fee, that is $3.60; the anti-farming check does not trip because no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 required, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.018, far below the 0.08 rate — so compensation is paid and, per POL-GEN-03, the emitted ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd of $3.60 while the rider's charge stands.

The POL-NS-09(d) escalation triggers are not met: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that would indicate rider abuse, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check on driver_profile does not trip (2 terminations against 4, and a 0.018 rate against 0.08), so neither limb of (d) sends this case to human review.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02731-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0 — no advisory covers this pickup road in the window — so POL-NS-06(i) interval-accumulation is unavailable and I do not rely on it; it is not needed, because the single in-geofence interval of 390 seconds already exceeds the 180 second minimum on its own, and the absent advisory therefore does not impair the arrival or dwell finding.
